# C++ code

How C++ is written in every Kokeb Labs repository: the language level, what the code may and may not use on a microcontroller, errors, naming and format. The pages under Standards explain the reasoning; this list is what CI and review hold each change to.

## KB-CPP-001: C++20, no compiler extensions { #kb-cpp-001 }

**MUST** · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0

Code is written in ISO C++20 and builds with `CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20`, `CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON` and `CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF`. Features beyond C++20 are not used.

*Why:* One language level across the stack lets any driver sit under any library. C++20 gives concepts and constexpr enough for zero-cost ports without the toolchain lag of C++23 on vendor compilers.

*Verified by:*

- `compiler-warnings/-Wpedantic` (implemented): the build is warning-free with the named flag and -Werror
- `forbidden-patterns/cmake-cxx-standard` (planned): a source scan for a construct the handbook bans; the parameter names the pattern set

*See also:* [ADR-0010](../adr/0010-cpp20.md); MISRA C++:2023 Rule 4.1.1 (the language standard is fixed)


## KB-CPP-002: No exceptions and no RTTI { #kb-cpp-002 }

**MUST** · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0

Code does not throw, catch or use `typeid` or `dynamic_cast`. Every target, including the exported library target, compiles with `-fno-exceptions -fno-rtti`.

*Why:* Exceptions and RTTI cost flash and RAM, are disabled on most embedded toolchains, and hide control flow that a safety review has to see. Errors travel as values (KB-CPP-004).

*Verified by:*

- `exceptions-rtti-off` (planned): the exported library target compiles with -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti, not only the tests
- `clang-tidy/cert-err58-cpp` (implemented): a clang-tidy check from config/.clang-tidy, run with the CMake compile database

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 18.1.1 (no exceptions in our profile); C++ Core Guidelines E.6


## KB-CPP-003: No heap in drivers; no heap after start-up anywhere { #kb-cpp-003 }

**MUST** · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0

Driver code never allocates from the heap. In libraries, HALs and firmware, dynamic allocation happens only during start-up, before the scheduler runs; after that no code calls `new`, `malloc` or anything that does.

*Why:* Heap fragmentation and allocation failure after start-up are failure modes that cannot be tested away. Fixed memory makes the worst case the normal case.

*Verified by:*

- `no-heap-link` (planned): a test binary that links the library with operator new, malloc and free removed builds and runs
- `clang-tidy/cppcoreguidelines-no-malloc` (implemented): a clang-tidy check from config/.clang-tidy, run with the CMake compile database
- `clang-tidy/cppcoreguidelines-owning-memory` (implemented): a clang-tidy check from config/.clang-tidy, run with the CMake compile database

*See also:* [ADR-0004](../adr/0004-no-heap.md); MISRA C++:2023 Rule 21.6.1 (dynamic memory should not be used); NASA/JPL Power of Ten Rule 3; SEI CERT C++ MEM51-CPP


## KB-CPP-004: Errors are values, and every result is used { #kb-cpp-004 }

**MUST** · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0

A function that can fail returns `<chip>::Result<T>` (drivers) or `kb::Result<T>` / `kb::Status` (above the drivers), marked `[[nodiscard]]`. A caller never discards a result; each layer boundary maps errors once.

*Why:* A bus error that is dropped turns into a stale reading. Typed results make the failure visible at every call and keep the original code for diagnostics.

*Verified by:*

- `compiler-warnings/-Wunused-result` (implemented): the build is warning-free with the named flag and -Werror
- `clang-tidy/bugprone-unused-return-value` (implemented): a clang-tidy check from config/.clang-tidy, run with the CMake compile database
- `compile-fail-tests` (implemented): a misuse of the public API is a compile error, proved by a test that must fail to compile

*See also:* [ADR-0001](../adr/0001-error-model.md); MISRA C++:2023 Rule 0.1.2 (the value returned by a function shall be used); SEI CERT C ERR33-C

*Explained in:* [standards/errors.md](../standards/errors.md)

## KB-CPP-005: Format with the org clang-format configuration { #kb-cpp-005 }

**MUST** · all · since 1.0

Every C and C++ file is formatted with the handbook's `config/.clang-format` (LLVM base, 2-space indent, 100 columns). Formatting is never argued in review; the tool decides.

*Verified by:*

- `clang-format` (implemented): clang-format with config/.clang-format; any difference fails

*Explained in:* [standards/naming-and-style.md](../standards/naming-and-style.md)

## KB-CPP-006: Names follow the org naming scheme { #kb-cpp-006 }

**MUST** · all · since 1.0

Types and public functions are `PascalCase`, private member functions `camelBack`, variables `snake_case`, private members `snake_case_`, constants and enumerators `kPascalCase`, namespaces `lower_case`, macros `UPPER_SNAKE`, exactly as `config/.clang-tidy` encodes it.

*Verified by:*

- `clang-tidy/readability-identifier-naming` (implemented): a clang-tidy check from config/.clang-tidy, run with the CMake compile database

*See also:* [ADR-0008](../adr/0008-naming.md)

*Explained in:* [standards/naming-and-style.md](../standards/naming-and-style.md)

## KB-CPP-007: No reinterpret_cast or C-style casts outside the port layer { #kb-cpp-007 }

**MUST** · driver, library, template · since 1.0

Driver and library code does not use `reinterpret_cast` or C-style casts. Register access that needs them lives in the MCU port, behind a function whose comment names the datasheet register.

*Verified by:*

- `clang-tidy/cppcoreguidelines-pro-type-reinterpret-cast` (implemented): a clang-tidy check from config/.clang-tidy, run with the CMake compile database
- `clang-tidy/cppcoreguidelines-pro-type-cstyle-cast` (implemented): a clang-tidy check from config/.clang-tidy, run with the CMake compile database

*See also:* MISRA C++:2023 Rule 8.2.5; C++ Core Guidelines Type.1


## KB-CPP-008: Static analysis is clean, and every suppression is a recorded deviation { #kb-cpp-008 }

**MUST** · driver, library, hal, firmware, template · since 1.0

clang-tidy and cppcheck report nothing. A finding on correct code is suppressed on its line with `NOLINT(<check>)` or `cppcheck-suppress <id>` and a reason; at the high and safety levels each suppression also has a deviation record (see Deviations).

*Verified by:*

- `clang-tidy/all` (implemented): a clang-tidy check from config/.clang-tidy, run with the CMake compile database
- `cppcheck/all` (implemented): cppcheck in strict mode; the parameter names the cppcheck message id
- review: Each new NOLINT or cppcheck-suppress names the check and says why the code is correct.

*See also:* IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 5.5.3 (software unit acceptance criteria)

*Explained in:* [deviations.md](../deviations.md)

## KB-CPP-009: Register frames have their layout asserted { #kb-cpp-009 }

!!! note "Proposed"

    Warns until 2027-03-01, then fails CI.

**MUST** · driver, library, hal (high level and above) · since 1.0 · enforced from 2027-03-01

A struct or union that mirrors a hardware register or a wire frame has `static_assert`s on its size and on the offset of every field, and states its byte order.

*Why:* Padding and byte order differ between compilers and targets; a silent layout change reads the wrong register.

*Verified by:*

- `register-layout-asserts` (planned): every register or wire frame struct has static_assert on its size and field offsets

*See also:* SEI CERT C EXP42-C


## KB-CPP-010: Data shared with an interrupt is atomic or explicitly guarded { #kb-cpp-010 }

**MUST** · driver, library, hal, firmware · since 1.0

A variable written in an interrupt handler and read elsewhere (or the reverse) is a lock-free `std::atomic` or is accessed only inside a critical section, and the function that runs in interrupt context says so in its documentation. `volatile` is for memory-mapped registers only, never for synchronisation.

*Verified by:*

- review: Every variable shared with an ISR is atomic or guarded, and the ISR-context function is documented as such.

*See also:* SEI CERT C SIG31-C; C++ Core Guidelines CP.8
